o1.biggest_strength: It puts the 46 to 90 day group first with no code, gives Monsoon Dark its own track and gates ex-subscribers on a delivery fix. Group counts are netted so nothing overlaps, and the profit table is worked from ₹557 and ₹442 per order.
o1.biggest_mistake: The Monsoon Dark email only sends people to a quiz and never names the closest match. It also hard-codes dates and a 'stopped in March' claim, and the whole piece is dense and probably over the 1,500-word limit.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name the closest match in the Monsoon Dark email, trim the length with plainer words, and state the break-even lift for each group.

o2.biggest_strength: It says plainly that people left because something broke, not over price. It names the match in the Monsoon Dark draft, gates ex-subscribers on on-time delivery, and ties each cancel reason to a fix.
o2.biggest_mistake: It starts with the 91 to 180 day group and treats the 9,000 at-risk customers at 46 to 90 days as a later day-28 nudge. That misses the cheapest win-back and leaves the first wave less sharp.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the 46 to 90 day group wave one with a light reminder, then fill the draft placeholders with real examples. Also work out the break-even lift for each group.

reason: Output 1 starts with the cheapest group, the 9,000 at 46 to 90 days, and covers every segment with its own offer, timing and exit rule. Its gross-profit working is the more cautious and checkable of the two. Output 2 is easier to read and its Monsoon Dark draft is better, but its order of targets is weaker.
